answer: A practical sybil defense is to anchor each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable stake: before an agent can vote or earn, it must lock a deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves. A hollow identity with nothing behind it carries no weight, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits. To keep the barrier fair the stake can be small yet scarce, like saffron, precious because it cannot be faked at scale, and honest agents recover it after a period of good behavior.
